name: Honey and ginger throat soothing

lead: A kitchen remedy used for throat comfort.
Honey has some cough evidence; ginger's effectiveness for any disease is uncertain.

paras: Proponents say honey coats and ginger soothes; mechanisms are not established in the sources reviewed.
Infant botulism risk with honey; ginger can interact with anticoagulants. [1][2]

lead: Honey and ginger throat soothing is a folk remedy of taking honey, ginger or both in warm drinks for throat comfort. A Cochrane review cited on Wikipedia found no strong evidence for or against honey for coughs, while the WHO recommends honey for coughs and sore throats. [1] Ginger has a long traditional medicine history, but its effectiveness for treating disease remains uncertain. [2]
infobox: Honey not recommended for infants under one [1]

paras: Evidence for honey easing children's cough is described as moderate to low quality. The UK MHRA suggests honey and lemon as a safer option than OTC cough medicine for children under six. Honey is not recommended before age one because of infant botulism risk. [1]
Ginger may help pregnancy nausea per low-quality evidence; it can cause heartburn, may interact with anticoagulants, and large amounts may cause GI discomfort. [2]
No studies found on honey and ginger for voice or vocal strain specifically; honey studies cover cough in general. [1]
